prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

MEXICO CITY, Mexico (CNN) -- The driver of a truck that collided with a bus in northeast Mexico, killing 12 people including 11 passengers from the United States and Canada, was intoxicated, a Mexican official said Tuesday. Emergency workers wheel a crash victim on a gurney after Monday's bus crash in Mexico. The tractor-trailer's 21-year-old driver was among those hospitalized after Monday's crash near Monterrey, Mexico, said Segismundo Doguin Martinez, a police official in the Mexican state of Coahuila. The driver of the bus was among those killed, and 15 bus passengers were injured. The Senda Express bus, operated by Grupo Senda, had been traveling from McAllen, Texas, carrying tourists to Zacatecas in central Mexico. Eight of those who died were from the United States, three were from Canada and one, the bus driver, was from Mexico, Doguin said.  Watch rescuers work at scene of deadly crash » . The survivors, most of them in grave condition, were taken to the Christus Muguerza Hospital and the Clinica La Concepcion, the Mexican official said. "They are in a delicate state but out of danger," Doguin said. El Milenio newspaper reported on its Web site that eight of the injured are from the United States, four are from Canada and three from Mexico. Seven of the injured Americans are from Texas and one is from Iowa, the newspaper said. El Norte newspaper's Web site and El Porvenir said the dead and injured included tourists. Among those killed in the crash was 73-year-old Ronald Christy, said his daughter, Pam Fordyce. Christy's wife, Margaret Christy, was in critical condition in a Mexican hospital, Fordyce said. "He was doing exactly what he loved -- traveling," Fordyce, of Altoona, Iowa, told CNN by telephone Tuesday. "He was right where he would want to be, on a bus." She said the couple wintered in Texas and lived in West Liberty, Iowa, in the summer. The U.S. consulate called her at 1:30 a.m. Tuesday to tell her that her father had been killed, Fordyce said, and then followed up with an e-mail with photographs of the crash. "I didn't even know he was on a bus," she said. "I guess I could believe [the consulate] when I talked to my brother" who knew the couple was traveling, she said. "Until then you don't want to believe anything." Doguin, the Mexican official, said the accident occurred when a truck driver went off the road and then overcorrected and swerved into oncoming traffic, hitting the bus. Video of the scene from CNN affiliate TV Azteca 13 showed the left side of the bus sheared off and the semi's cab completely flattened. Rescue efforts took five hours, TV Azteca 13 reported. The U.S. consulate in Monterrey will not release the names of the dead or injured until all family members have been notified, said consulate spokesman Todd Huizinga. "On Monday evening, staff from the consulate in Monterrey went to the Christus Muguerza Hospital to offer assistance to some of the injured who were brought there after the crash," Huizinga said. "The consulate expects to have more detail in the coming hours." The truck driver was injured and is being held by authorities at a hospital, Doguin said. The Web site for Grupo Senda says the company started in Linares, Mexico, more than 75 years ago. It provides bus service to 15 Mexican states and the Texas Valley, the site says. Elizabeth Suarez, director of the McAllen Central Bus Station, where the bus trip originated, issued a statement saying, "We are very saddened by the news this morning. We offer our condolences to the families. The city of McAllen is the landlord of the bus terminal facility in McAllen. Grupo Senda is our tenant." CNN's Melanie Whitley, Taylor Gandossy, Tess Eastment and Monica Trevino contributed to this report from Atlanta, Georgia.

outputs.L1:
**MEXICO CITY, Mexico (CNN) —** The driver of a truck that collided with a bus in northeastern Mexico, killing 12 people—including 11 passengers from the United States and Canada—was intoxicated, a Mexican official said Tuesday.

Emergency workers transported a crash victim on a gurney following Monday’s bus accident near Monterrey, Mexico.

The 21-year-old driver of the tractor-trailer was among those hospitalized after the crash, said Segismundo Doguin Martinez, a police official in the Mexican state of Coahuila. The bus driver was among those killed, and 15 bus passengers were injured.

The Senda Express bus, operated by Grupo Senda, had been traveling from McAllen, Texas, carrying tourists to Zacatecas in central Mexico. Of those killed, eight were from the United States, three were from Canada, and one—the bus driver—was from Mexico, Doguin said.

**Watch rescuers work at the scene of the deadly crash »**

The survivors, most of whom were in grave condition, were taken to Christus Muguerza Hospital and Clinica La Concepcion, the Mexican official said.

“They are in a delicate state but out of danger,” Doguin said.

El Milenio newspaper reported on its website that eight of the injured were from the United States, four were from Canada, and three were from Mexico. Seven of the injured Americans were from Texas, while one was from Iowa, the newspaper said.

The websites of El Norte and El Porvenir reported that tourists were among the dead and injured.

Among those killed was 73-year-old Ronald Christy, according to his daughter, Pam Fordyce. Christy’s wife, Margaret Christy, was in critical condition at a Mexican hospital, Fordyce said.

“He was doing exactly what he loved—traveling,” Fordyce, of Altoona, Iowa, told CNN by telephone Tuesday. “He was right where he would want to be, on a bus.”

She said the couple spent winters in Texas and lived in West Liberty, Iowa, during the summer.

The U.S. Consulate called Fordyce at 1:30 a.m. Tuesday to inform her that her father had been killed, she said, and later followed up with an email containing photographs of the crash.

“I didn’t even know he was on a bus,” she said. “I guess I could believe [the consulate] when I talked to my brother,” who knew the couple was traveling. “Until then, you don’t want to believe anything.”

Doguin said the accident occurred when the truck driver veered off the road, overcorrected, and swerved into oncoming traffic, striking the bus.

Video of the scene from CNN affiliate TV Azteca 13 showed the left side of the bus sheared off and the semi-truck’s cab completely flattened. Rescue efforts took five hours, TV Azteca 13 reported.

The U.S. Consulate in Monterrey will not release the names of the dead or injured until all family members have been notified, said consulate spokesman Todd Huizinga.

“On Monday evening, staff from the consulate in Monterrey went to the Christus Muguerza Hospital to offer assistance to some of the injured who were brought there after the crash,” Huizinga said. “The consulate expects to have more detail in the coming hours.”

The truck driver was injured and was being held by authorities at a hospital, Doguin said.

Grupo Senda’s website states that the company was founded in Linares, Mexico, more than 75 years ago. It provides bus service to 15 Mexican states and the Texas Valley, according to the site.

Elizabeth Suarez, director of the McAllen Central Bus Station, where the trip originated, issued a statement saying: “We are very saddened by the news this morning. We offer our condolences to the families. The city of McAllen is the landlord of the bus terminal facility in McAllen. Grupo Senda is our tenant.”

CNN’s Melanie Whitley, Taylor Gandossy, Tess Eastment, and Monica Trevino contributed to this report from Atlanta, Georgia.
outputs.L2:
MEXICO CITY, Mexico (CNN) — A 21-year-old tractor-trailer driver was under the influence of alcohol when his vehicle struck a passenger bus in northeastern Mexico, leaving 12 people dead, including 11 travelers from the United States and Canada, a Mexican official said Tuesday.

Emergency personnel were seen moving one of the victims on a stretcher following Monday’s collision near Monterrey.

Segismundo Doguin Martinez, a police official in Coahuila state, said the truck driver was hospitalized after the wreck. Authorities were holding him at the hospital while he received treatment.

The bus operator was killed, and 15 passengers suffered injuries. The vehicle, a Senda Express bus run by Grupo Senda, had departed from McAllen, Texas, and was transporting tourists to Zacatecas in central Mexico.

According to Doguin, the fatalities included eight Americans, three Canadians and the Mexican bus driver.

Most of the survivors were in serious condition and were transported to Christus Muguerza Hospital and Clinica La Concepcion, Doguin said. Although he described their conditions as delicate, he added that they were no longer in danger.

The newspaper El Milenio reported online that the injured included eight U.S. citizens, four Canadians and three Mexicans. Seven of the injured Americans were reportedly from Texas, while one was from Iowa. The websites of El Norte and El Porvenir said tourists were among both the dead and the wounded.

One of those killed was 73-year-old Ronald Christy, according to his daughter, Pam Fordyce. She said Christy’s wife, Margaret, remained in critical condition at a Mexican hospital.

“He was doing exactly what he loved — traveling,” Fordyce, who lives in Altoona, Iowa, told CNN by telephone Tuesday. “He was right where he would want to be, on a bus.”

Fordyce said her parents spent winters in Texas and summers in West Liberty, Iowa. She learned of her father’s death when the U.S. Consulate called her at 1:30 a.m. Tuesday. The consulate later sent an email containing photographs of the wreck.

“I didn’t even know he was on a bus,” she said. Fordyce added that she was able to accept what the consulate had told her only after speaking with her brother, who knew the couple had been traveling. Until that point, she said, she did not want to believe the news.

Doguin said the crash happened after the truck left the roadway. Its driver then overcorrected, veered into the opposite lane and collided with the bus.

Footage from CNN affiliate TV Azteca 13 showed that the bus’s left side had been torn away and that the semi-truck’s cab had been crushed flat. The station reported that rescue operations lasted five hours.

Todd Huizinga, a spokesman for the U.S. Consulate in Monterrey, said officials would not identify the dead or injured until every family had been informed.

Huizinga said consular employees went to Christus Muguerza Hospital on Monday evening to assist some of those taken there after the collision. He added that the consulate expected to obtain further information within the following hours.

Grupo Senda’s website says the company was founded in Linares, Mexico, more than 75 years ago. It operates bus routes in 15 Mexican states as well as the Texas Valley.

Elizabeth Suarez, director of McAllen Central Bus Station, where the journey began, released a statement expressing sorrow over the accident and offering condolences to the victims’ families. She noted that the city of McAllen owns the bus terminal property and that Grupo Senda leases space there.

CNN’s Melanie Whitley, Taylor Gandossy, Tess Eastment and Monica Trevino contributed to the report from Atlanta, Georgia.

counterfactuals.output:
# 12 Killed After Truck Collides With Tourist Bus in Coahuila, Mexico

**Eight Americans, three Canadians and the Mexican bus driver were killed; authorities say the 21-year-old truck driver was intoxicated**

**COAHUILA, Mexico —** Twelve people were killed when a truck driven by an allegedly intoxicated 21-year-old collided with a tourist bus in the northern Mexican state of Coahuila, authorities said.

The dead included eight U.S. citizens, three Canadian citizens and the bus’s Mexican driver. Officials had not publicly identified the victims pending notification of their families.

Emergency crews responded to the crash and worked to secure the wreckage, assist survivors and recover the victims. Authorities had not immediately provided a confirmed number of injured passengers or details about their conditions.

Investigators detained the truck driver, who authorities said showed signs of intoxication. Toxicology testing and other forensic examinations were expected to determine the driver’s blood-alcohol level and whether alcohol was a direct factor in the collision. No final determination of criminal responsibility had been announced.

Officials were also examining the vehicles, roadway conditions, speed and available surveillance or dashboard-camera footage. It was not immediately clear which vehicle crossed into the other’s path or whether mechanical failure contributed to the crash.

The U.S. and Canadian governments were expected to coordinate with Mexican authorities to confirm the victims’ identities, notify relatives and assist with the return of their remains. Consular officials had not yet released further information.

Mexican prosecutors could pursue serious criminal charges if investigators determine that intoxication or reckless driving caused the deaths. Under Mexican law, the detained driver is presumed innocent unless convicted.

Authorities urged relatives seeking information to contact local emergency services or their country’s nearest consular office rather than travel directly to the crash site.

The investigation remains active, and officials said additional information would be released after families had been notified.
